content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use this, that, these, and those while comparing clothes. Model: “These trousers are small, but that skirt is the right size.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use this size or that size clearly and politely. One useful response is: “These trousers are small, but that skirt is the right size.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where this size or that size is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

exercises.prompt: Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about this size or that size.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about this size or that size.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.

language_focus: Use this, that, these, and those while comparing clothes.
objectives: Use this, that, these, and those while comparing clothes.
Use demonstratives and sizes in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about this size or that size.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about this size or that size. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: Which item is right?
listening.transcript: These jeans are too long. That skirt is small, but this one is right.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Contrast this /ðɪs/ and these /ðiːz/. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about this size or that size.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using this size or that size; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise this size or that size?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: These trousers are small, but that skirt is the right size.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about this size or that size with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about this size or that size. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: These trousers are small, but that skirt is the right size. Submit your draft first.
